The Reserve Bank ​of India likely intervened ‌in the foreign ​exchange market ⁠on Tuesday (September 15, 2026), four traders told Reuters, as rising ‌oil prices and growing wagers ‌on a ‌rate ⁠hike in the ⁠U.S. this week pressured the South Asian unit.
The ​rupee declined ‌0.2% to 95.79, hovering around its weakest levels in ‌a month.

State-run banks ​were spotted offering dollars, most ⁠likely on behalf of the RBI, the ‌traders said. The dollar sales were not “especially heavy” in nature and are likely ‌intended to limit excessive volatility, ​a trader at a Mumbai-based ⁠bank said.
Brent crude oil prices ⁠were last up 1.2% ‌at $106.9 per barrel.
